messages.content: Can you send to Mom an Email saying we should go out and play if Friday is okay.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to send emails directly. However, I can help you draft a message that you can copy into your email client. Here’s a suggestion:

> Subject: Friday Plans  
> Hi Mom,  
> Would you be free to go out and play this Friday? Let me know what time works best for you.  
> Love, [Your Name]

Feel free to tweak it to match your style!
message.reasoning: The user wants to send an email to Mom asking if Friday is okay to go out and play. We need to use the function get_current_weather? No, that's not relevant. There's no function to send email. So we cannot do it. According to policy, we can respond with a refusal or partial compliance. We can't send email. We can offer to draft the email text. That would be partial compliance. So we refuse to actually send but provide a draft.
